_comment: The design families, and the ONLY place their flags are written down.
build.ps1 builds from this file and check_design_sets.py verifies the
built sets against it, so there is no second copy to drift. It used to be
five pasteable commands in README.md, which cost three separate people a
session: a <dst> placeholder PowerShell rejects as a reserved operator, a
$dst variable it silently expands to nothing (building to the DRIVE ROOT),
and two pasted in parallel, which corrupt each other's cache entries.
EVERY FLAG IS LOAD-BEARING. A set is selected at load time by hidden,
intermediate, gated_ffn AND the datapath, so a set built with the wrong
flags is not a slower design -- it is one the wrong model loads, or none.
Both directions of that have already shipped wrong once.
_common_note: --tg-depth 2 software-pipelines the runtime sequence's task groups: worth
1.034-1.141x of array time, bit-identical. --tg-depth 3 compiles clean and
then TIMES OUT on hardware, reproducibly. 2 is the maximum that runs.
--batches IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE, and moving it in was a correctness fix
-- FAMILY ARGS FIRST, common LAST -- and argparse takes the LAST occurrence
of a repeated flag, so a family's own --batches would be silently
overridden by common's. The build completes, prints ok, and produces a
design with the wrong tiers: which is exactly the BERT-h1024-bfp16 defect
in check_design_sets.py's own docstring, and undetectable from the artifact
because a design with the wrong tiers is a perfectly valid design. It
lives in each family's own args now, so one place per family means a
family can set its own without a precedence fight between two readers that
Four tiers on the BERT families, because use_tier() picks the smallest that
fits and falls back to the largest: a single tier pads every request to
batch 128, measured at 18.3x on a single text. Upstream's bge-large still

families.name: BERT-h384-bf16
families.note: THE ONE FAMILY WITH NEITHER --emulate-bfp16 NOR --c-bf16. bge-small failed the bfp16 MTEB gate at -0.5010 bit-reproducibly, so it stays on the plain datapath, and its C stays fp32. Adding --c-bf16 here builds a design that loads and is not the one that passed the gates -- which shipped once.

families.name: BERT-h768-gated-bfp16
families.note: One set for two models: their GEMM geometry matches bit for bit. Note also that qkv and attn_out here are IDENTICAL to BERT-h768-bfp16's -- neither depends on --gated-ffn or --intermediate -- so these two families share 8 of their 16 cache markers and must never be built concurrently.

families.name: BERT-h1024-bfp16
families.note: -n 32, not 48: the design asserts N % (tile_n * n_cols) == 0 and bge-large's N is in {1024, 3072, 4096}. 64 divides them but needs 65,536 B of a 63 KB L1 budget.

families.name: BERT-h768-gated-i1152-bfp16
families.note: laya-multilingual's ENCODER: mmBERT-base, hidden 768 with intermediate 1152 rather than the 3072 every other hidden-768 family here carries, so ffn_up is 2304 wide and ffn_down consumes K=1152. -n 48 is legal for all four N values (2304, 768, 2304, 768) and matches every shipping family, so this is an ORDINARY new geometry rather than a forced one -- which is the whole reason it is a new family and not a variant of BERT-h768-gated-bfp16. Its qkv (768x2304) and attn_out (768x768) are BYTE-IDENTICAL to BERT-h768-bfp16's, since neither depends on --gated-ffn or --intermediate: those two families share 8 of their 12 cache markers and must never be built concurrently. --seq 1024 because that is laya-multilingual's own max_len, and the host attention running alongside it is O(seq^2). Tiers 4,16,32 rather than the usual 4,16,32,128 because at seq 1024 a batch-64 tier materialises batch x heads x seq^2 x 4 = 3.2 GB of scores on the host. There is NO tier 1: export_gemm_rtp.py requires every tier to be a multiple of 4, so a single row runs a four-row pass and pays 4x the host attention for it. DATAPATH IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT AN INHERITANCE: this is the --emulate-bfp16 arm and the -bf16 arm below differ in exactly that flag, and the accuracy gate picks one. bge-small failed its MTEB gate on bfp16 at -0.5010 bit-reproducibly and had to be rebuilt on plain bf16, so this is not a formality.

families.name: BERT-h768-gated-i1152-bf16
families.note: The same geometry on the plain bf16 datapath: no --emulate-bfp16, everything else identical. It is a SEPARATE FAMILY rather than a flag override for two reasons: check_design_sets.py keys on emulate_bfp16, which is the one field that differs in design.json, so reusing one name would make the checker report the second build as a stale set of the first; and both have to be able to sit in src/xclbins at once for the accuracy gate to A/B them. `serves` is empty until that gate picks: whichever wins gets the tag and the other stays built for the next checkpoint of this shape.
